Senses.Note: Four appraisals from four independent works establish the eye-exchange image as a reversal of who sees and who is deceived.

Occurrences.Kwic: 黃龍心云：直下穿過髑髏，已是換却眼睛。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X66/X66n1297.xml). Dharma Grove of the Tradition’s Mirror. Huanglong Huinan says that penetrating straight through the skull has already exchanged the eyes.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X66/X66n1296.xml). Compilation of the School Gate’s Raising Old Cases. Baiyan Fu says people claim the gandharva king had his eyes exchanged by the golden ascetic, while the Buddha had his eyes exchanged by the king even more severely.

Senses.Explanation: To have one’s eyes exchanged is to undergo a reversal in which the supposed observer loses command of seeing. Chan case critics use the grotesque image when a word, gesture, or opponent covertly replaces a person’s eye and leaves that person deceived or reoriented. Huanglong Huinan says that penetrating straight through the skull has already exchanged the eyes. Baiyan Fu says both the gandharva king and the Buddha have their eyes exchanged by the other party. An identified Fahua master warns that even a foreign shipmaster would have to exchange his eyes. A source-record speaker says Nansen, Zhaozhou, and the hermit exchange the eyes of anyone whose eye of the Way is unclear.
